One week later, his laboratory values are within normal limits. This patient's condition was most likely caused by damage to which of the following structures?

                    ### Question
                    Two days after undergoing an emergency laparotomy following a motor vehicle collision, a 37-year-old man has increased thirst. Examination shows dry mucous membranes and decreased skin turgor. A review of his chart shows his urine output to be in excess of his fluid intake. Laboratory studies show a serum sodium concentration of 151 mEq/L and urine osmolality of 110 mOsmol/kg H2O. One hour after the administration of desmopressin, the serum sodium concentration is 146 mEq/L and urine osmolality is 400 mOsmol/kg H2O. One week later, his laboratory values are within normal limits. This patient's condition was most likely caused by damage to which of the following structures?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Posterior pituitary
opb. Adrenal cortex
opc. Proximal renal tubule
opd. Collecting duct
ope. Supraoptic nucleus

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Damage to the posterior pituitary likely caused decreased secretion of antidiuretic hormone (ADH), leading to decreased water reabsorption in the kidneys. This resulted in dehydration symptoms, hypernatremia, and concentrated urine. Administration of desmopressin normalized serum sodium concentration and urine osmolality, resolving the symptoms. The evidence paths do not provide direct support for the specific cause of the condition in this patient.
